reason: The cited lines only parse arguments, call pulls.getPullRequest(owner, repo, pull_number), and return the resulting pull request JSON as text. They do not show arbitrary host code execution or writing/sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination. They also do not establish that the returned pull request is non-public or accessed with user credentials, so SECRET is insufficient. Pull request data is repository/user-supplied content, and the lines show it is returned to the agent, so UNTRUSTED is supported.
